Method: two-sided Welch independent-samples t-test  (data version v2; Python: scipy.stats.ttest_ind(group_1='treatment', group_2='control', equal_var=False, alternative='two-sided'); confidence_interval(confidence_level=0.95))
H0: Δ = 0 versus H1: Δ ≠ 0, where Δ = μ(group = treatment) − μ(group = control) for the mean of outcome; α = 0.05

| Group | n | Mean | SD |
|---|---|---|---|
| treatment | 25 | 1.22 | 0.69 |
| control | 24 | -0.05 | 0.85 |

Mean difference = 1.27 (95% CI 0.82 to 1.71); t(44.50) = 5.722; p < 0.0001
Decision at α = 0.05: reject_H0
Distribution checks (descriptive only, never used to choose the method): [{'check': 'shapiro_wilk', 'variable': 'outcome', 'group': 'treatment', 'n': 25, 'shapiro_wilk_p': 0.16838955839373165}, {'check': 'shapiro_wilk', 'variable': 'outcome', 'group': 'control', 'n': 24, 'shapiro_wilk_p': 0.5366741918967267}]

A total of 25 records were analysed in the treatment group and 24 records in the control group. Welch's test result: t(44.50) = 5.722, p < 0.0001. The decision at 0.05: we reject H0. The estimated mean difference (treatment minus control) is 1.27, with a 95% confidence interval ranging from 0.82 to 1.71. The treatment group's sample mean was higher than the control group's sample mean. That this is an association only when groups were not randomized.

Limitations:
- Random allocation was not established. This analysis describes an association and does not establish causation.
- User-confirmed exclusions include missing values. The missingness mechanism is unknown; complete-case analysis may be biased and generalizability is limited.
- Inference is conditional on the stated independent observations and the method's distribution and model assumptions; descriptive checks do not prove these assumptions.
